question: Provide a broad company research overview covering the business and revenue mix; financial snapshot and trajectory; balance sheet, debt and working capital; operating cash flow and cash conversion; management narrative versus reported numbers; explicit guidance and capital allocation; and a concise bull and bear case. Include material governance concerns, auditor qualifications, contingent liabilities and related-party risks where supported. State source periods and consolidated versus standalone scope. Identify missing evidence without inventing a four-quarter or multi-year comparison.

report.title: TCS Company Research Overview

findings.statement: TCS reports revenue across multiple industry verticals for FY 2026, led by Banking, Financial Services and Insurance at 38.7% and total segment revenue of ₹ 267,021 crore.
Geographic revenue distribution for FY 2026 is concentrated in North America at 48.6%, followed by the United Kingdom at 17.4% and Continental Europe at 15.4%.
Operating profit reached ₹ 66,838 crore in FY 2026 with an operating margin of 24.6%.
Earnings per share increased to ₹ 145.99 in FY 2026, with a 10.3% CAGR over the past five fiscal years.
In Q2FY27, revenue was ₹ 73,188 crore, growing 2.8% year-on-year in constant currency.
Order book TCV for Q2FY27 was US$ 9.6 billion, excluding the Porsche and Best Buy deals.

On a consolidated basis as of March 31, 2026, non-derivative financial liabilities include trade payables of ₹ 14,808 crore, lease liabilities of ₹ 13,218 crore, and other financial liabilities of ₹ 11,227 crore.

Related-party transactions on a standalone basis include inter-corporate deposits given to Tata Capital Limited (₹ 1,000 crore) and Tata Capital Housing Finance Limited (₹ 500 crore) as of March 31, 2026.
TCS highlights prudent working capital management leading to consistently high cash conversion.
Management highlights strong deal momentum and client commitment to multi-year transformations, supported by a Q2FY27 TCV of US$ 9.6 billion.
Management explicitly states that the company does not provide any specific revenue or earnings guidance.
The bull case is supported by strong profitability, scaling capabilities in AI-led engineering, disciplined capital allocation, and broad-based large deal wins.
The bear case involves risks such as litigation provisions (including US$ 112 million for trade secret misappropriation claims), wage increases, intense competition, and macroeconomic uncertainties.

report.title: Reliance Industries Limited Research Brief

findings.statement: Reliance operates across segments including O2C, Oil and Gas, Retail, Digital Services, and Others, generating external turnover of ₹1,071,174 crore in 2024-25 on a consolidated basis.
Retail business performance was supported by network expansion, opening 1,564 stores during FY 2025-26 to reach a total store count of 20,160 stores.
On a consolidated basis, Net Profit Margin increased from 6.3% in FY 2024-25 to 8.0% in FY 2025-26, and Return on Capital Employed increased from 14.6% to 20.7%.
Retail segment revenue from operations (net of GST) reached ₹3,28,202 crore in FY 2025-26, up from ₹2,91,043 crore in FY 2024-25, with EBITDA of ₹27,034 crore.
S&P raised RIL's rating from BBB+ to A- in December 2025, reflecting rising contribution from less cyclical, consumer-facing businesses.
On a consolidated basis, Debt Service Coverage Ratio increased from 2.06 in FY 2024-25 to 4.03 in FY 2025-26, and Interest Coverage Ratio increased from 5.59 to 8.83.
Consolidated Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities was ₹1,92,113 crore for FY 2025-26 compared to ₹1,78,703 crore for FY 2024-25.
Standalone Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities was ₹79,059 crore for FY 2025-26 compared to ₹79,392 crore for FY 2024-25.

Management expects benefits to start accruing in absolute EBITDA from next year onwards regarding margin frameworks, noting that online retail has lower capital investment requirements compared to offline businesses.
Regarding power capacity, management stated that 44 megawatts is being processed to be completed in the next four to six months, with a planned 120-megawatt addition taking some time.

The bull case is supported by an S&P credit rating upgrade to A- reflecting a rising contribution from less cyclical, consumer-facing businesses, and strong growth in retail store footprints and digital commerce capabilities.

The bear case or risk elements include high judgments involved in Level 3 fair value measurements for specific fibre assets under Ind AS 113, and competitive intensity requiring continued margin investments in customer acquisition.
